title: The distinction of flesh and the meaning of bones
english: Having taken the distinction from the soul, it is troubled by the opposite of death. 'All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as the flower of grass' (Ps 103:15). Again he says, 'All flesh shall come unto thee' (Ps 22:27), that is, every man. 'All flesh shall see the salvation of our God' (Ps 22:29). All things that are homonymous are divided from those having the same name by the addition of certain [elements]. If it is said in the Scripture, 'He who gives food to all flesh,' we hear of every living creature by nature. But if I say, 'I will pour out from my spirit upon all flesh,' I speak of receiving the bestowed gift of spirit.

4 There is no peace to my bones from the face of my sins (Ps 32:3), because I see my sins present. But not everyone takes understanding of the face of them, but he who repents and wishes to flee them. The one sinning and being ignorant of this very thing that he sins, does not see the face of his sins, nor does he see their shame. But the one perceiving those things which he does, and seeing that he performs them according to the transgression of divine commands, has the face of the sins appearing to him.

He does not say 'bones' of the body in every way, except according to the lowestly understanding, just as it was also said concerning flesh. And it has been said in those preceding: 'All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like unto thee?' (Ps 73:26). If the bones say, 'Lord, who is like unto thee?', they have received the understanding of the Lord and of His form, so as to know that no one is like Him. For the likeness toward God and the unlikeness [which brings] knowledge of God and theology makes [it] manifest; so that he does not speak concerning the bones of the body, but concerning the strong and firm dogmas of the soul and its powers; for then the sensible bodies are held together by the bones; for it was not possible to have nerves and veins and the rest, if he did not have bones. Where [is it said]: 'There is no peace to my bones?'—when the powers of the soul follow one another, they are at peace. When the soul does not divide...
the calculating faculty, the desiring faculty
